speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand your condition, please tell me when these symptoms started and if the pain radiates to your arm, jaw, or back.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome.

The combination of forceful vomiting following excessive alcohol intake, followed by choking, coughing, and subsequent chest pain in a 51-year-old male is highly suggestive of a spontaneous esophageal rupture. I have determined the diagnosis based on the classic clinical presentation; no further questions or tests are required.
